name: Dale Strong

items.text: On October 23, 2020, the Madison County Commission, which Strong chaired, had a Confederate monument moved from the courthouse grounds to a cemetery. The Alabama Attorney General said this broke the state Memorial Preservation Act and sued. A $25,000 fine was paid and the suit was dismissed. County lawyers said an undisclosed third party paid it, not taxpayers.
items.why: The Attorney General's determination was about a commission decision with no personal gain, and a court never ruled on it, so it does not clearly fail the abuse-of-office criterion (6).

items.text: In November 2019, three Madison County volunteer fire chiefs told WAFF that Strong, the commission chairman and a Monrovia volunteer firefighter, used his influence to favor Monrovia in county budgets. Monrovia led all volunteer stations by over $130,000. Strong said Monrovia pays more property tax and so gets more back. He said he recommends funding but the commission votes on the budget.
items.why: This is an unresolved accusation of favoring his own community's fire station (criterion 6), with no official finding and a tax-based explanation from Strong.

for_review: I found nothing on Strong on the owner's named sites; the one search returned only unrelated Alex Jones and Infowars news. Item 1: The Attorney General's release says Madison County paid the $25,000. County lawyers said in a court motion that an undisclosed third party paid it, so the sources conflict. Wikipedia says Strong called the move necessary for the monument's structural integrity, and a WHNT piece quotes him on a private donor paying the fine. I could not open the WHNT page (alabamas42.com copy) and found no other source for the structural-integrity claim, so neither is in the text. Also unverified: the unanimous commission vote, and that Strong was chairman in October 2020, which Wikipedia reports. The AG's lawsuit filing itself was not opened. Item 2: The WAFF page was cut off partway through. Its later parts, and any official audit or follow-up on county fire funding, were not read. Strong's 2020 funding figures (Monrovia over $300,000 versus $43,000 for another station) came only from a search snippet. Attendance was not weighed.
